summary: Glacier County lookout (Hudson Bay Divide, also Divide Mountain): 1931 house wrecked by wind, 1934 replacement lost to wind by 1937; foundation remains per register.

facts.design: Octagonal lookout (register); steel tower (lookout history page)
facts.status_note: Wind destroyed the 1934 lookout by 1937. The register says the 1931 foundation remains as of 2022.
facts.agency: National Park Service (Glacier National Park); Blackfeet Nation as cooperator

events.note: Ready-cut 14 by 14 lookout house built in June 1931 on Divide Mountain. The register dates the foundation to 1931.
A November 1931 windstorm demolished the lookout house.
An August 1932 report planned to pay an observer on the point from July 25 to about September 10. Planned in the report; not confirmed as done.
Second lookout built at the site. The register calls it octagonal; a lookout history page calls it a steel tower.
The lookout blew over in 1937. A Glacier archives photograph of wind wreckage is dated June 25, 1937.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register calls the site Divide Mountain; the Glacier archives and the lookout history page call it Hudson Bay Divide. Dates and wind loss line up, so the story treats them as one lookout. No source names both explicitly.
Lookout history page gives 7138 ft; the register gives 7,677 ft (2,340 m). The story gives neither figure.
The register describes the 1934 lookout as an octagon; the lookout history page calls it a steel tower. The story reports both descriptions.

The lookout history page says the 1934 structure blew over in 1937; the register says the 1931 foundation remains and the structure was destroyed by wind. The story keeps these as two separate structures and the foundation as the remaining feature.

notes_for_editor: The brief's source URL (hudsonsbaydivide.html) returns 404; the working page is hudsonbaydivide.html. Identity of Hudson Bay Divide and Divide Mountain is inferred from matching dates (1931 house, 1934 replacement, wind loss) and the Glacier County location; no source names both. The brief's coordinates (48.66869, -113.38604) are about 1 km from the register point (48.670851, -113.400402, my calculation). The register gives elevation 7,677 ft; the history page gives 7138 ft. Access today is not described by any source. The 1931 house was not rebuilt until 1934 per the sources, so the 1931 and 1934 structures are treated as separate.
